all souls: ‘indeed the church in its pilgrim members, from the very earliest days of the christian faith, has honoured with great respect the memory of the dead; and ‘because it is a holy and a wholesome thought to pray for the dead that they may be loosed from thei r sins.’ (2 mac:12-46), she offers her suffrages for them. these consist, primarily, in

the celebration of the eucharist, and prayers for the dead, alms deeds, works of mercy, and the application of indulgences to the souls of the faithful departed’. (directory of popular piety and the liturgy, 251) tuesday - st. malachy: was born near armagh in 1094. he became vicar of ceallach, the reforming bishop of armagh., and he continued his work to reform as bishop of connor. he founded the monastery of mellifont and established the canons regular into ireland. in 1148 malachy set out from ireland to meet the pope but died on his way at clairvaux, where he caught fever and died in the arms of bernard and is buried in the abbey church. wednesday - st. charles borromeo (1538 - 84): cardinal archbishop of milan at the age of twenty-one, worked for reform in his diocese, drafting the catechism of the council of trent. patron saint of catechists and seminarians. thursday - st. martin de porres (1579 – 1639): became a dominican lay-brother, spending his nights in prayer and penance, his days in the monastery, caring for the sick and the poor. he is renowned for his devotion to the blessed sacrament. friday - all the saints of ireland: ‘in the communion of saints, many and varied spiritualities have been developed throughout the history of the churches … the different schools of christian spirituality share in the living tradition of prayer and are essential guides for the faithful. in their rich diversity the are refractions of the one pure light of the holy spirit.’ (ccc,2684) saturday - st. willibrord: was born in northumbria in 658. he entered the benedictine order and was sent to study, including spending twelve years, 678 - 690, at the monastery of rath melsigi, near milford, co carlow before going, with eleven companions, to evangelise frisia. he established a session of ulrecht and in 695 was ordained archbishop of ulrecht by pope serguis i. he founded a monastery of ech ternach in luxemburg in 700, where he died in 739. diocesan vocations: for the future priests of our diocese, the men who will preach the good news of the beatitudes (today's gospel) - (more information will follow). fr. crowley a warm welcome to fr james devine. we are delighted to extend a very warm welcome to fr james devine, who has been appointed to serve in kilrea & desertohill, errigal and granaghan. note from fr. james - thank you all for welcoming me to the parishes this weekend. my name is fr james devine, and i grew up in the waterside area of derry. i was ordained to the priesthood on the 8th december 2013, in st columba's church, long tower, derry. i have four siblings: three older brothers and one younger sister. as a priest, i have served in the parishes of limavady and holy family, ballymagroarty, with a three-year stint in the usa with the marian fathers of the immaculate conception between these two appointments. my most recent appointment has been in the parish of greencastle, co. tyrone, where i had three very happy and fruitful years. i look forward to joining you all in the parishes of granaghan, kilrea and desertoghill, and errigal, and pray that i can be a faithful priest for you, along with fr crowley. we wish fr james every blessing as he begins his ministry among us. let us keep him in our prayers and give him our wholehearted support, not only through our words of welcome, but through our presence, our encouragement and our active participation in the life and mission of the parishes in this area in which he will serve. fr. crowley parish safeguarding: vetting process will take place on the first saturday of every month after the vigil mass. this will be to re-vet all existing volunteers as a new requirement from the diocese. if you are over 18 and volunteer as a sacristan /choir leader /children’s liturgy helper or baptism group helper for the parish please attend a meeting, on saturday 7th

(gauge also available on website and facebook page). thanks - donations to date - current figure £235,400.00. providing compassionate care at the end of life - to address the sensitive issue of compassionate care at the end of life, and in response to the need to inform the faithful of catholic teaching on this important life issue that affects so many families, the bishops of ireland have published the pastoral letter: freedom to live fully, until death comes. you are invited to read this letter and view the accompanying video through the valley, which offers personal testimonies by carers and people with terminal illness. the key message of both letter and video asserts that every person possesses inherent, infinite dignity that remains intact regardless of their circumstances. in this context, bishops strongly oppose the oireachtas committee’s proposal to government to legislate for assisted suicide and call on support for healthcare workers who uphold the sanctity of life. to read freedom to live fully, until death comes and to watch through the valley, visit the following link:
